title: Managing extreme AI risks amid rapid progress
pitch: Twenty five leading scientists, including three Turing Award winners, warn that AI may soon outpace our ability to control it, and set out what research and governance must do now.

chapters.g: The case in brief: rapid progress, serious risks, and a plan.
Why AI could soon match or exceed humans in many areas, and why it need not stop at human level.
Harms from misuse, social injustice and loss of human control over autonomous systems.
Research priorities: oversight, robustness, interpretability, evaluations and resilience, with a third of AI research budgets for safety and ethics.
Institutions, government insight, safety cases and mitigation rules scaled to risk.

ideas: AI progress could soon outpace safety.
Loss of human control is a real risk.
At least a third of AI R&D should go to safety and ethics.
Governments need oversight institutions with real power.

args.a: Leading scientists see extreme risks as near enough to act now.
args.c: Others, including some top researchers, think such risks are far off or overstated.

args.a: Developers should prove their systems safe with safety cases.
args.c: Industry worries about cost and slowing innovation.

questions: Why might AI not stop at human level?
Is a third of research budgets for safety the right share?
Which governance measure would help most?
